newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Petrovietnam still talking with refinery partners.
newsitem.headline: Petrovietnam still talking with refinery partners.

text.p: Petrovietnam's board chairman Ho Si Thoang said on Tuesday Vietnam was doing its own feasibility study for the country's first oil refinery, but was not ruling out foreign involvement in the project.
"We did not reject anything or anybody," he told Reuters in response to an official news agency report which said Vietnam would build the refinery itself. "But the project must move forward."
Thoang said Petrovietnam had received a letter from one of the prospective partners, South Korea's LG Group, expressing the company's continued desire to be involved.

He added that if the foreign firms were unwilling to participate directly in the $1.4 billion project as partners, possibilities remained for them to be involved in other aspects such as infrastructure construction.
Earlier, the official Vietnam News Agency quoted Petrovietnam's director general as saying that Vietnam would build the refinery alone.
"Vietnam willl build the nation's first-ever oil refinery at Dung Quat in Quang Ngai central province by itself," it quoted Ngo Thuong San as saying.

Petrovietnam's partners in a feasibility study were South Korea's LG Group, Stone & Webster, Malaysia's Petronas, U.S. refiner Conoco and Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corporation and China Investment Development Corp.
